newsitem.title: USA: US drug group slips after Pfizer earnings.
newsitem.headline: US drug group slips after Pfizer earnings.

text.p: Shares in U.S.-based pharmaceutical companies fell Wednesday following slightly lower-than-expected second quarter earnings reported by Pfizer Inc.

Analysts expressed concerns on how foreign exchange, which reduced Pfizer's worldwide revenue growth by four percent in the quarter, would affect other U.S. drug companies as their earnings are released in the next two weeks.
Late Tuesday Pfizer reported $0.35 per share earnings for the second quarter, $0.01 short of the First Call consensus estimate. Its stock was off 2-3/16 to 59-1/2.
Eli Lilly fell 3-7/16 in the Pfizer undertow to 113-7/16. Warner-Lambert Co was off 1-11/16 to 138.
Merck & Co, which reports earnings Thursday, was down 1-11/16 to 98-7/8. American Home Products was off 3/4 to 80-1/2.
But two British-based drug companies were gainers, with Glaxo Wellcome Plc up 12/16 to 47-5/16 and Smithkline Beecham Plc up 11/16 to 104-15/16.

Mario Corso, pharmaceuticals analyst for Rodman & Renshaw, said Pfizer's worldwide sales growth of nine percent was one or two percentage points less than analysts had predicted, even excluding the negative foreign exchange effect.
"The sales were just a little bit less than people thought they would be," he said, due in large part to disappointing sales of Pfizer antidepressant Zoloft and the antibiotic Zithromax.
He said year-on-year Zoloft sales grew at nine percent for the quarter, rather than by mid-teen expectations.
And he said although Zithromax sales rose 16 percent over 1996's second quarter to $158 million, sales represented a decline from the $264 million seen in the first quarter of 1997.
"That was a large falloff and shows that maybe wholesalers were stocking up last quarter," Corso said.
He said Pfizer's earnings were also somewhat disappointing because they came up short in spite of more favorable tax treatment this quarter.
"Pfizer's tax rate in the first quarter was 30 percent, but it fell to only 27.5 percent this quarter," Corso said.
